name: Stern v. Marshall
summary: The Supreme Court held that a bankruptcy court — a non-Article III court — could not enter final judgment on a state-law counterclaim that did not stem from the bankruptcy proceeding itself, because doing so would improperly exercise the judicial power reserved to Article III courts.
significance: Establishes that Article III limits Congress's ability to strip federal courts of jurisdiction over claims that are traditionally resolved in courts of law, relevant to whether monetary H-2A enforcement claims belong in agency or Article III proceedings.
